implicit_requirement: Connections created through the discrete SQLite configuration mode must preserve the repository's SQLite foreign-key enforcement behavior.
Database connections created from the new discrete MySQL settings must support execution of the repository's existing multi-statement migration units.
The new discrete MySQL runtime configuration path must preserve temporal-column decoding compatible with repository scanners.
Discrete MySQL runtime connections must preserve identifier semantics compatible with the repository's existing runtime SQL.
The poll-history entry point must remain unavailable in repository-defined video rooms where message-history actions do not apply.
When a command accepts a newly expanded duration syntax, its user-facing help must describe both unit-bearing durations and the retained bare-millisecond fallback.
When the duration parser rejects input supplied through the command interface, the failure must be translated into the command framework's normal user-facing error channel.
A resource created for delayed command scheduling must be released if scheduling fails before the resource is successfully activated.
A syntactically valid duration that exceeds the scheduling backend's representable range must fail through the established user-command error boundary.
An asynchronous audit path must deliver every accepted buffered event in the same order in which the events were accepted.
Failure to deliver one buffered audit event must not terminate forwarding of later accepted events while the asynchronous emitter remains active.
Enabling browser CSRF protection must preserve authenticated non-browser write clients that are not exposed to ambient-cookie CSRF.
Client-held CSRF state established through one protected route family must be scoped so that the same state is available to every protected route family that subsequently validates or consumes it.
A browser client subject to the configured request-forgery validation must receive a usable request proof corresponding to its protected session.
The browser client must acquire and retain the server-issued request-forgery proof during initialization before protected API mutations are sent.
Protected browser API mutations must return the acquired request-forgery proof through a request channel accepted by the server validator.
Existing application metric instruments must emit through the telemetry provider selected during startup configuration.
Deployments that omit the new metrics configuration must remain metrics-enabled unless they explicitly disable metrics.
Every response resource obtained from the repeated external team-membership request must be released on both successful and error-status paths.
A provider transport failure during team-membership retrieval must abort authentication and remain distinguishable from a negative membership decision.
A malformed successful membership response from the external provider must be treated as an operational failure rather than as a valid empty-membership result.
Reusing a shared retrieval path for artist albums must preserve the established result ordering of the existing artist-specific query.
Adding album-genre relations must preserve retrieval of albums that have no corresponding genre-relation records.
Refactoring album queries to use common options must preserve the existing valid no-option random-album invocation.
Adding optional genre associations to album refresh must not exclude media or albums that have no genre association.
Fallback-cache entries must be partitioned by every request identity dimension that determines the underlying resource result.
Certificate-authority reads that include signing material must not enter the ordinary shared fallback cache.
Values returned from a shared fallback cache must not expose mutable state that one caller can alter for later callers.
A public paginated listing operation must reject a nonpositive page limit even when listing is served through a cache or fallback path.
Cached node results must be ordered lexically by resource name before cursor-based pagination is applied.
Paginated reads served from a fallback cache must resume at the lexical lower boundary represented by a non-empty continuation key.
Only resources satisfying requested filters may consume positions in the requested result-page limit.
A full page reconstructed from cached nodes must return a continuation cursor that resumes strictly after the last node emitted on that page.
During a backend failure, the fallback cache must suppress immediate repeated loads for the same key for a bounded interval.
A supported environment-lifecycle command that clears tsh-managed selection state must also clear the Kubernetes-cluster selection introduced through the new environment-variable input.
Generated shell-environment output must carry the currently selected Kubernetes cluster so that later client invocations preserve that selection.
An explicitly supplied site selection must retain precedence over either or both site-related environment values.
A local OCI-backed store must retain immediate location validation at construction even when fresh retrieval targets are created for later operations.
A snapshot subscription must close its caller-provided output channel before returning when the established subscription contract assigns completion signaling to the implementation.
The new module must load and behave consistently across the repository's supported interpreter range, including its legacy lower bound.
The new module must resolve its shared platform helpers in both source-tree development/testing and installed-package execution layouts.
A route identified by partition and name must cross the remote member-resource boundary in that API's accepted partition-qualified key representation.
A route-existence check must map every supported BIG-IP not-found representation to resource absence.
A new remote-management module must accept the shared provider and connection parameters required to reach and authenticate to its target device.
When the route partition is not supplied directly, the module must honor the repository-standard environment source before falling back to the default partition.
Advisory identity must be derived according to the originating distribution feed's identifier representation rather than by applying another feed's title rule.
Advisory-resolution lookup for a modular package must use the stream-qualified component identity defined by the feed rather than only the plain package name.
The document-format version introduced by the feature must use 1.0 as its current semantic identifier across export and import.
Documents created before version metadata was introduced must remain importable when their version field is absent.
Requested namespace creation during import must apply only to a nonempty custom effective namespace, never to the built-in default namespace.
Long-lived success cache metadata must be attached only after artwork retrieval succeeds; request-validation and retrieval failures must not be advertised as cacheable artwork responses.
Every producer of the shared artist-image URL field must emit the same new public-route identity contract.
Adding a new dark-mode implementation variant must preserve a valid preferred-color-scheme mapping for that variant.
At the established evaluation-store boundary, cached rollout retrieval must conform to the existing method type, preserving its typed rollout collection and error-return contract.
Smart-playlist rules over user-scoped annotation fields must be evaluated only against annotations belonging to the current user.
Playlist-track mutations must be permitted only for an administrator or the playlist's named owner, with lookup failure and every other principal denied before mutation.
For every supported playlist replacement size, each generated storage write must remain within the backend's statement or argument capacity.
After a successful playlist-track replacement or smart refresh, the persisted song count must equal the number of tracks in the resulting materialized playlist.
After a successful playlist-track replacement or smart refresh, persisted playlist duration must equal the aggregate duration of the current materialized tracks.
After a successful replacement or refresh of materialized playlist membership, the persisted playlist byte-size aggregate must equal the aggregate byte size of the current materialized tracks.
When an operation changes a playlist's materialized membership, the playlist's persisted modification state must record that change.
A Trivy report with no result entries must be rejected as unsupported rather than emitted as a successful scan result.
Each accepted Trivy parser result must preserve the established exact ingestion-channel value "trivy" in its ScannedVia output contract.
Directional placement normalization must preserve the established hidden-state value at the consumer-visible placement boundary.
For the same ordered registered-device set, the compatibility projection consumed by legacy single-device clients must preserve the device selection made by the pre-feature server behavior.
A multi-device authentication-challenge request must return an explicit not-found outcome when no registered device yields a challenge, rather than succeeding with an empty challenge set.
A decoded authentication payload containing no challenge in any supported representation must be rejected before device authentication begins.
The new logging setting must participate in the repository's standard environment-backed configuration channel with its established source precedence.
The dedicated gRPC logging control must use the repository's established application logging-level vocabulary and severity meanings.
An invalid dedicated gRPC logging level must prevent successful startup and return actionable context identifying the rejected configuration.
Extending shared expression parsing must preserve the resolvable source-argument dependency required by existing email-local expressions.
Extending the shared expression walker must preserve the established local-part transformation semantics of email.local for existing consumers.
Regular-expression string arguments must preserve the expression language's established quoted-string and escape semantics before regular-expression interpretation.
A role-bearing work-author entry must remain valid under the established typed author-relation contract while adding optional role metadata.
Adding contributor-role extraction must preserve the established non-role personal-author projection for the same MARC input.
A contributor's work-specific role must not alter matching to that contributor's shared author identity across works.
A contributor role that applies to one work must not be persisted as a global attribute of the shared author entity.
Cross-process display events must use an IPC transport compatible with the multiprocessing context used by the worker processes and existing event channel.
When display events extend the shared worker-to-controller final-queue protocol, every recognized pre-existing event variant must retain its established observable semantics.
Overlay-scrollbar support decisions must follow the capabilities of the loaded Qt runtime rather than unrelated compiled binding versions.
On platforms that cannot support the new overlay mode, selecting or defaulting to it must preserve the previous search-sensitive scrollbar behavior.
When no user override exists, scrolling.bar must resolve to overlay as the product default.
Dynamic JavaScript-header scenarios must run on Qt runtimes where the capability is functional and be suppressed only throughout the known broken interval from Qt 5.12 through 5.14.
Structured logging mode must preserve machine-readable startup discovery for each enabled service endpoint and must not announce endpoints that are disabled.
When file and environment configuration both provide a logging encoding, the environment value must take precedence consistently with the repository's configuration-source contract.
Changing log representation must leave the deployment's configured logging destination effective for ordinary logger-mediated records.
Changing log representation must preserve the configured threshold for ordinary application records.
An explicitly supplied configuration path must take precedence over automatic discovery and default fallback.
A configuration-path probe failure other than ordinary absence must remain distinguishable to operators before fallback continues.

Default fallback must be limited to the absence of a selected configuration source; failures while reading, decoding, or validating a selected source must remain observable and prevent silent startup with defaults.
Adding optional configuration loading must preserve diagnostics produced by a successfully loaded configuration file.
Each request for default configuration must yield configuration state that can be mutated independently of every other request.
All fixed user-visible copy introduced by the new token-entry view must remain available to the repository's localization process.
User-controlled room names must retain content-appropriate bidirectional text direction when rendered in the revised header.
Moving room identity within the header must preserve its status as the page's level-one accessible heading.
Extending the shared gain parser with a new metadata format must preserve acceptance of existing valid values containing surrounding separator whitespace.
R128 track and album gain lookup must remain independent of the letter case used by raw metadata keys.
When a focal author-name query returns a redirect record, the candidate must resolve to its terminal canonical author identity before matching or fallback author creation.
An orderly telemetry-worker shutdown must not discard a report that the reporting path has already accepted as successful but has not yet delivered.
Loading the wrapper-selection machinery during early startup must not import or select a Qt wrapper before wrapper arguments and early error handling are available.
A fatal startup diagnostic produced before the primary graphical framework is usable must remain visible in both graphical-launch and terminal/headless modes.
Risky in-process native wrapper loading during early startup must occur only after crash reporting or equivalent containment is available.

After early explicit wrapper selection succeeds, later existing wrapper imports must consume that selection without restarting it or treating the implicit call as a conflicting explicit initialization.
Every supported vulnerability-data acquisition mode must produce equivalent unified first-class semantics for both exploited-vulnerability sources.
Segmenting a verification-code control into multiple native inputs must preserve a valid target for the existing wrapper label.
A component that expands one public verification-code control into multiple native controls must give every simultaneously rendered control an unambiguous document identity.
Every positional accessible name introduced for the segmented verification fields must participate in the application's localization pipeline.
Segmented verification-code entry must prevent browser text-assistance behavior from transforming or annotating literal code characters.

The anonymous share-page bootstrap must expose only the established public track projection: identifier, title, artist, album, update time, and duration, rather than the full internal media representation.
Anonymous consumption of a public share must not make share creation or share-management listing available without caller authentication.
A share created through an authenticated management request must be attributed to that authenticated creator.
An unauthenticated public-share capability must resist practical enumeration of unrelated shares.
Adopting the shared multipart serializer must preserve the existing server-facing checksum and artifact-part wire contract used for collection publication.
Multipart upload metadata must expose a client-facing filename without disclosing directory components from the underlying local or remote file path.

An ordinary request that names a controller-local source must continue to resolve that source, make it available to managed-host execution through a usable staged reference, and close the managed temporary-resource lifecycle under established policy.
The generalized uri action flow must preserve direct managed-host source execution when a request declares remote_src.
Newly staged multipart content must remain subject to the framework's established access policy for potentially private remote temporary files.
Multipart content staged on a managed host must be removed after every ordinary synchronous success or failure, except when established asynchronous or explicit-preservation policy retains it.
Applying Raspbian-specific package filtering for vulnerability detection must not mutate the caller-owned canonical package inventories.
Using a package-filtered scan view for detection must not prevent newly detected vulnerability state from being retained in the caller-owned canonical scan result.
A newly selected nonempty custom client-storage root must support first profile and credential writes without requiring the user to create the root beforehand.
Relocating profile storage must preserve one compatible identity, indexing, and path relation between profile metadata and its credentials across all producers and consumers.
Relocating profile and credential storage must not weaken the access restrictions applied to the same stored material at the default location.
When callers do not supply language candidates, language resolution must use the repository's authoritative current language registry.
When no usable image-count evidence exists, an import must not assert a fabricated positive page count.
Manual route-target reconciliation must not mutate the target device when the module operates in check mode.
When a check-mode request contains a manual route-target delta that would alter device configuration, the module must report that a change is pending.
The shared full-width security card must remain contained within the device-details layout after its padded and bordered presentation is introduced there.
A language name that matches multiple canonical language records must not be assigned arbitrarily and must instead be rejected through the established import-validation boundary.
Matched-record enrichment with newly normalized language values must preserve existing valid language metadata while adding normalized values that are not already present.
Importing an alias for a language already stored on an edition must not append a second reference to the same canonical language.
A failed user-chain creation or deletion must be reported as a failed module operation rather than successful lifecycle completion.
The newly added user-chain lifecycle operations must remain limited to the current runtime firewall state unless persistence is separately requested.
Adding optional firewall-chain lifecycle management must preserve the established precedence and meaning of flush and chain-policy requests.
When scanning a remote target, every supported scanner path must exclude loopback destinations that refer to the scanner host rather than the remote target.
Failure during any setup, option-conversion, or execution stage of an external scan must be reported as scan failure rather than a successful empty result.
When an external scan omits an optional technique, execution must still select a runnable default compatible with the configured privilege mode.

When external port scanning is used for an IPv6 endpoint representation already accepted by the existing scan pipeline, the endpoint must be submitted in an IPv6-compatible form and successful results must remain associated with that same endpoint.
Open endpoints discovered by an external scanner must be translated into identities semantically compatible with the existing reachability-correlation path.
Extending the existing SmartBanner to another supported product must preserve established click observability when a user activates its app-store link.
A banner click must be attributed to the same product identity represented by the clicked banner and its destination.

Adding index completion must preserve the tab-focus argument contract: non-integer values are limited to last, stack-next, and stack-prev, and every other string is rejected as an invalid value before focus execution.
Extending the shared tab-completion helper for active-window filtering must preserve the existing all-window result scope of callers that request no filter.
Generalizing buffer enumeration must preserve the existing transfer completion's exclusion of buffers already belonging to the source window.
Index-oriented tab completion must preserve current tab-index order rather than sorting displayed index strings lexicographically.
Removing the core terminal-input dependency must preserve construction of supported legacy third-party connection plugins that still require the former constructor input.
Seeking within an advertised playback range must not dereference a chunk playback object that is still unavailable because asynchronous preparation has not completed.
Importing a result with supported operating-system metadata must preserve the source result's concrete operating-system family identity.
When the extended importer processes a supported-OS Trivy result, the emitted scan result must preserve the source target as its established server and report identity.

Routing supported-operating-system Trivy results through common metadata processing must preserve the established scanner-origin and target-provenance contract, or migrate all affected producers and consumers to an equivalent contract.
Existing alias expansion and accepted partial-command resolution must complete before an input is classified as an unknown command and a replacement is suggested.
Consolidating backend feature arguments must preserve every unrelated user-supplied, configured, and generated backend argument without dropping, duplicating, or changing its relative order.
Existing producers that omit the newly optional workflow status must continue to enter the established pending state.
Bibliographic records entering the shared import pipeline must be validated against the required-field semantics of the canonical import contract.
Records produced from the external bibliographic source must carry a stable source-specific identity shared by replay deduplication and later source lookup.
Resumable multi-file processing must preserve a deterministic candidate-file identity and order across runs so that a stored active filename denotes the same remaining work after restart.
Valid records from the bulk metadata source must enter a pre-promotion workflow state that excludes them from automatic import consumption.
The importer must exclude records belonging to the developer-designated independently-published source class before batch submission.
The new bibliographic importer must reject records whose publication year is later than the current year, consistently with the repository's established import-quality policy.
A resumable batch importer must not advance its durable checkpoint beyond records that have been successfully accepted for submission.
Watcher event-size telemetry must retain numeric size observations without making each distinct observed size a persistent metric-series identity.
Watcher telemetry must process supported resource-less control events without breaking the watch stream because their resource payload is absent.
Watcher-event metrics must aggregate resource-bearing events by a stable bounded resource-category identity rather than per-instance object identity.
Generalizing the request counter for new watcher statistics must preserve the established interval-frequency semantics of existing backend and cache request reports.
An absent, malformed, or empty watcher-event metric family must degrade to empty telemetry without making the existing monitoring report unusable.
Generalizing histogram projection for watcher data must preserve component-specific series selection for all existing backend and cache latency reports.
The flat path-suggestion model must report no descendants beneath an existing item.
Plugin-state validation must accept the complete repository-recognized plugin identifier domain while rejecting identifiers outside that domain.
A newly emitted localized error identifier must resolve to readable administrator-facing feedback in every supported locale path.
A new internal package dependency must resolve to the co-versioned repository-local workspace package used by the implementation.
A render-duration measurement must correlate its completion event with the same logical item identity used to start that measurement.
Email content render-time measurement must begin at the user's mailbox-item selection before downstream lookup, retrieval, composition, navigation, or rendering work.
A telemetry lifecycle may proceed only when a usable identity is available to correlate its start and completion to one selected item.

Each completed email-content render-time measurement must classify whether the target content was already cached when measurement began and serialize that classification within the metric schema's bounded boolean-label domain.
Each logical render-readiness measurement lifecycle must contribute at most one completion observation, even when its readiness or completion signal is delivered repeatedly.
An ECRT completion may emit a duration sample only when it correlates to a prior start for the same logical lifecycle.
Each valid completed ECRT lifecycle must submit one positive sample to the registered ECRT metric sink.
Each render-timing sample must carry the actual initiating mailbox location in the metric schema's bounded location domain.
Each email content render-time sample must carry the page-size class applicable to its mail setting within the telemetry schema's bounded domain.
Each completed content-render-time sample must represent elapsed duration from mailbox-item selection to content render readiness.
A valid external-link destination must remain recoverable for security processing when a supported browser's ordinary anchor access path fails but equivalent href data is still available.
User-facing URL-extraction failure feedback must remain available through the repository's supported localization path.
A newly supported rule shape must retain one equivalent rule identity across presence checks, creation, insertion, deletion, and non-mutating preview.
The newly supported set-matching behavior must be available with equivalent semantics through both existing IPv4 and IPv6 rule backends.
Independent ignore rules may coexist only with an omitted manifest configuration, and must conflict with every explicitly supplied manifest value, including explicit falsy values.
Omitting manifest configuration must keep the default collection build independent of any optional dependency used only for explicit manifest processing.
A newly generated default collection configuration must leave the optional manifest mode inactive until the user deliberately enables it.
The seasonal reading-goal prompt must test for a goal in the campaign target year: the upcoming year in December and the current year in January and February.
The recurring My Books campaign window must use December 1 as its opening boundary and February 1 of the following year as its closing boundary.
Every supported month-and-day range shape must include dates equal to either named endpoint.
Adding external profiles must keep routine public author-page rendering from depending on an uncontrolled live Wikidata request for each visit or ordinary cache miss.
The initial statement-derived external-profile rollout must expose exactly the developer-approved service set: Google Scholar, while deferring other social or profile properties.
Each Google Scholar external profile must derive its destination from the corresponding Wikidata Scholar identifier using Scholar's canonical author-profile addressing contract.
Each icon-only external-profile link must expose a programmatically determinable name that identifies its target profile or service.
User-facing action names introduced for external-profile links must remain translatable through the repository's supported localization path.
A variable number of required external-profile links must remain contained and reachable within the bounded author-information surface when they exceed one row.
Every browser-facing profile icon in the bounded initial rollout must be delivered through an Open-Library-controlled origin rather than directly hotlinked from a third-party image host.
Author candidates obtained at any matching stage must be resolved to their canonical terminal author before selection and attachment.
Author candidates returned by an identifier query must be materialized without issuing a separate database fetch for every returned author.
When several existing authors match incoming remote identifiers, the author supported by the greatest number of equal supplied identifiers must be selected before applying any equal-score tie rule.
When candidate authors have equal remote-identifier support, resolution must deterministically prefer the lower numeric local author identifier.
Author-import matching and conflict checks must cover every identifier type recognized by the authoritative author-identifier registry rather than a fixed example subset.
Extending author inputs with identifier-bearing records must preserve the established person-record conversion semantics for legacy string authors.
Structured provider-supplied author labels entering identity matching or author creation must not be passed through a lossy normalizer intended for unstructured fallback text.
When the bundled provider obtains an Open Library author identity from Wikidata, it must use the value defined by Wikidata's Open Library author-ID property.
Every external identifier emitted by provider enrichment must be labeled with a canonical remote-identifier key that denotes the same identifier service as the source property.
Structured-provider lifespan timestamps must be converted to the repository's year-level date representation before name/date matching or author storage.
An external Open Library author identifier must be canonicalized into a valid repository author key before direct key lookup.
The cached-child count must reflect raw cache membership independently of whether each child's presentation-ready representation is currently available or fresh.
A cached-child count queried during rendering must be a synchronous, side-effect-free read of current scoped cache membership.
A resolved user's WebFinger self link must label the actor representation with the exact media type required by established ActivityPub consumers.
Both user and instance-actor discovery success paths must remain subject to the endpoint's configured global discovery-visibility authorization policy.
When message creation fails, the client must leave the submitted content available in a retryable composer state whose content-derived state remains consistent.

The migrated message-create path must preserve condition-appropriate error routing: recognized actionable failures receive equivalent specialized recovery, and all remaining failures are visibly reported.
After an edit request fails, the client must preserve a coherent retryable edit context for the same target message and attempted content.
Migrating an existing message-edit operation to a new client transport must preserve user-visible reporting when an edit request is rejected.
An edit or delete request for a nonexistent message must receive the specific invalid-message outcome before message-dependent policy or mutation processing occurs.

The flat path-suggestion model must report no descendants beneath an existing item.
Plugin-state validation must accept the complete repository-recognized plugin identifier domain while rejecting identifiers outside that domain.
A newly emitted localized error identifier must resolve to readable administrator-facing feedback in every supported locale path.
A new internal package dependency must resolve to the co-versioned repository-local workspace package used by the implementation.
A render-duration measurement must correlate its completion event with the same logical item identity used to start that measurement.
Email content render-time measurement must begin at the user's mailbox-item selection before downstream lookup, retrieval, composition, navigation, or rendering work.
A telemetry lifecycle may proceed only when a usable identity is available to correlate its start and completion to one selected item.

Each completed email-content render-time measurement must classify whether the target content was already cached when measurement began and serialize that classification within the metric schema's bounded boolean-label domain.
Each logical render-readiness measurement lifecycle must contribute at most one completion observation, even when its readiness or completion signal is delivered repeatedly.
An ECRT completion may emit a duration sample only when it correlates to a prior start for the same logical lifecycle.
Each valid completed ECRT lifecycle must submit one positive sample to the registered ECRT metric sink.
Each render-timing sample must carry the actual initiating mailbox location in the metric schema's bounded location domain.
Each email content render-time sample must carry the page-size class applicable to its mail setting within the telemetry schema's bounded domain.
Each completed content-render-time sample must represent elapsed duration from mailbox-item selection to content render readiness.
A valid external-link destination must remain recoverable for security processing when a supported browser's ordinary anchor access path fails but equivalent href data is still available.
User-facing URL-extraction failure feedback must remain available through the repository's supported localization path.
A newly supported rule shape must retain one equivalent rule identity across presence checks, creation, insertion, deletion, and non-mutating preview.
The newly supported set-matching behavior must be available with equivalent semantics through both existing IPv4 and IPv6 rule backends.
Independent ignore rules may coexist only with an omitted manifest configuration, and must conflict with every explicitly supplied manifest value, including explicit falsy values.
Omitting manifest configuration must keep the default collection build independent of any optional dependency used only for explicit manifest processing.
A newly generated default collection configuration must leave the optional manifest mode inactive until the user deliberately enables it.
The seasonal reading-goal prompt must test for a goal in the campaign target year: the upcoming year in December and the current year in January and February.
The recurring My Books campaign window must use December 1 as its opening boundary and February 1 of the following year as its closing boundary.
Every supported month-and-day range shape must include dates equal to either named endpoint.
Adding external profiles must keep routine public author-page rendering from depending on an uncontrolled live Wikidata request for each visit or ordinary cache miss.
The initial statement-derived external-profile rollout must expose exactly the developer-approved service set: Google Scholar, while deferring other social or profile properties.
Each Google Scholar external profile must derive its destination from the corresponding Wikidata Scholar identifier using Scholar's canonical author-profile addressing contract.
Each icon-only external-profile link must expose a programmatically determinable name that identifies its target profile or service.
User-facing action names introduced for external-profile links must remain translatable through the repository's supported localization path.
A variable number of required external-profile links must remain contained and reachable within the bounded author-information surface when they exceed one row.
Every browser-facing profile icon in the bounded initial rollout must be delivered through an Open-Library-controlled origin rather than directly hotlinked from a third-party image host.
Author candidates obtained at any matching stage must be resolved to their canonical terminal author before selection and attachment.
Author candidates returned by an identifier query must be materialized without issuing a separate database fetch for every returned author.
When several existing authors match incoming remote identifiers, the author supported by the greatest number of equal supplied identifiers must be selected before applying any equal-score tie rule.
When candidate authors have equal remote-identifier support, resolution must deterministically prefer the lower numeric local author identifier.
Author-import matching and conflict checks must cover every identifier type recognized by the authoritative author-identifier registry rather than a fixed example subset.
Extending author inputs with identifier-bearing records must preserve the established person-record conversion semantics for legacy string authors.
Structured provider-supplied author labels entering identity matching or author creation must not be passed through a lossy normalizer intended for unstructured fallback text.
When the bundled provider obtains an Open Library author identity from Wikidata, it must use the value defined by Wikidata's Open Library author-ID property.
Every external identifier emitted by provider enrichment must be labeled with a canonical remote-identifier key that denotes the same identifier service as the source property.
Structured-provider lifespan timestamps must be converted to the repository's year-level date representation before name/date matching or author storage.
An external Open Library author identifier must be canonicalized into a valid repository author key before direct key lookup.
The cached-child count must reflect raw cache membership independently of whether each child's presentation-ready representation is currently available or fresh.
A cached-child count queried during rendering must be a synchronous, side-effect-free read of current scoped cache membership.
A resolved user's WebFinger self link must label the actor representation with the exact media type required by established ActivityPub consumers.
Both user and instance-actor discovery success paths must remain subject to the endpoint's configured global discovery-visibility authorization policy.
When message creation fails, the client must leave the submitted content available in a retryable composer state whose content-derived state remains consistent.

The migrated message-create path must preserve condition-appropriate error routing: recognized actionable failures receive equivalent specialized recovery, and all remaining failures are visibly reported.
After an edit request fails, the client must preserve a coherent retryable edit context for the same target message and attempted content.
Migrating an existing message-edit operation to a new client transport must preserve user-visible reporting when an edit request is rejected.
An edit or delete request for a nonexistent message must receive the specific invalid-message outcome before message-dependent policy or mutation processing occurs.
